https://www.thesun.co.uk/news/22277342/p.title: ACTIVIST ARRESTS More than 50 people suspected of planning to disrupt coronation arrested
https://www.thesun.co.uk/news/22277342/p.text:
ANTI-monarchists and eco-zealots suspected of planning to disrupt the Coronation were among at least 52 people arrested today.
The head of anti-royalist group Republic, Graham Smith, was among six held at Trafalgar Square as they tried to unveil placards.
Also held was Patrick Thelwell, 23, who was convicted of flinging eggs at King Charles in York in November last year.
Hundreds of protesters were there, chanting “Not my King”.
But they were shouted down by patriotic royalists chanting back: “He’s my King”.
Republic director Henry Stratton said: “They were carrying placards that were saying 'not my King' when around 20 police said 'we are stopping you and we are searching you'.
“After that they arrested them saying 'we are seizing all these placards' and Graham said 'why are you arresting us?'”
In one video an officer said: “I'm not going to get into a conversation about that, they are under arrest, end of."
Police earlier arrested 14 people from Just Stop Oil in East London in a planned swoop.
Others were held in The Mall, Whitehall and along the procession route.
Most arrests were for conspiracy to cause public nuisance and to prevent a breach of the peace.
One man was held on suspicion of possessing a knife and drugs in The Mall and another for sexual assault in Trafalgar Square.
Campaign group Liberty said the arrests “set a dangerous precedent for us as a democratic nation”.
The Met hailed the success of their policing operation.

image.caption: Police arrested 14 people from Just Stop Oil in East London in a planned swoop

https://www.thesun.co.uk/news/22422630/i.title: HOTEL HELL Inside massive abandoned ‘ghost hotel’ in Brit hols hotspot as 21-storey, 400 room resort left to rot for 20 years
https://www.thesun.co.uk/news/22422630/i.text:
RISING high over the picturesque Spanish coastline in a holiday hotspot popular with Brits is an enormous abandoned hotel branded a "monstrosity".
The so-called Ghost Hotel of Algarrobico has been sitting half-built for nearly 20 years just metres from the coastline in the Cabo de Gata National Park.
Almeria is the third most popular region of Spain for UK expats and welcomes 2million tourists each year  - and those who explore its beautiful coastline may have stumbled across the eerie structure.
It stands 21-storeys tall and was planned to have more than 400 rooms with stunning sea views and swimming pools just a stone's throw from the beach.
Three cranes even still stand on the site - frozen in time from the day workmen downed tools for the last time.
Work on the towering structure began in 2003 by the Spanish company Azata.
But what followed was 20 years of rows with environmental activists and the national park authority which left the hotel's shell sitting abandoned - having never opened its door to holidaymakers.
The hotel is located just 50 feet from the shoreline and was hoped to be a statement resort for the area.
But after three years of controversial construction all development was halted back 2006.
Environmental activists lobbied to have the hotel project shut down as it was being built on the national park's protected land.
The hotel row has in the intervening 17 years been dragged through the courts some 20 separate occasions.
Local press branded the hotel a "monstrosity".
And with the row ongoing, just last month Carboneras Council declared the land the hotel is built on as "undevelopable".
It paves the way for the structure to be demolished after sitting unoccupied for nearly two decades, reported Murcia Today.
The hotel has become an eyesore and stand derelict, still littered with construction equipment, covered in graffiti and being battered by the coastal winds.
Knocking down such an enormous structure however poses a new wave of challenges for locals.
"How the Algarrobico hotel can still exist is a mystery, but unfortunately the truth is that it is not an isolated case," Pilar Marcos, a biologist from Greenpeace, told The New York Times.
However, while many believe such an enormous structure should never have been built in such as beautiful area - others feel like it's reputation is slowing down on all other development in the region.
Cato de Gata is popular with tourists - but there no accommodation with more than 45 rooms within the park's borders.
And other developers have said the abandoned monster is impacting attempts to bring in more tourists and drive the local economy.

"The Algarrobico was a giant aberration that has unfortunately stigmatized any kind of new economic activity in this whole area," said Ivan García, who wants to open a boutique hotel.
"If nobody creates jobs around here, we will not protect this beautiful area but instead allow it to depopulate completely and die off."

https://www.thesun.co.uk/news/22261810/p.title: PIERS MORGAN After decades of inexorable decline in power and influence, today Great Britain will again be the envy of the world
https://www.thesun.co.uk/news/22261810/p.text:
Life’s not been an easy ride lately for Britons.
There was a time when Britain led the world in almost everything – from inventing the steam engine, telephone, and computer, to having the best writers (Shakespeare, Dickens), bands (the Beatles and Rolling Stones), language (English), spies (James Bond) and politicians (Churchill).
We truly did justify the ‘Great’ in Great Britain, and punched way above our weight class as we bestrode the global stage.
There was a tremendous pride in being British.
Watch Piers Morgan Uncensored weekdays on Sky 522, Virgin Media 606, Freeview 237, Freesat 217 or on Fox Nation in the US
But after many decades of inexorable decline in our power and influence, pretty much all we’ve got left to boast about is being No1 for being monitored by CCTV cameras, sarcasm, drinking tea, queuing, and laziness. (Yes, a recent survey revealed more Brits would quit all work, if money wasn’t an issue, than any other nationality.)
In the past few years, we’ve endured the horribly divisive Brexit referendum, a disastrous pandemic in which we fared worse than any other major European country in terms of death toll and financial fall-out, the worst cost-of-living crisis in memory, a ruinous war in Ukraine that sparked serious food shortages and surging energy prices across the continent, rocketing violent crime, an NHS on its knees, the pound tanking to virtual parity with the dollar thanks to Liz ‘Lettuce’ Truss, illegal migration across the channel worsening, and in a true symbol of how far we’d fallen, it was revealed that we’ve also pumped record torrents of raw sewage into our seas and onto our coastlines.
As I wrote after that last stinking shame was exposed, this seemed to cement most people’s sense that the country was literally going to sh*t.
And then the great Queen Elizabeth II, our magnificent rock of stability for over 70 years, died, plunging the country into mourning and a palpable sense of national fragility.
But strangely, in her passing, the Queen gave the world a vivid reminder of what Britain still does better than anywhere else on the planet, and that’s our Monarchy and all the pomp, pageantry and glorious military procession that goes with it.
Her funeral, televised to hundreds of millions around the world, was a tremendously soul-stirring illustration of the regal ‘soft’ power that only we can do.
And the way the country put its differences aside to come together and pay heartfelt tribute to this iconic lady who meant so much to so many of us, showed that whenever the going gets tough, Britain will always dust itself down, and unite to rally to the cause.
The now legendary Queue of people who lined up to pay silent homage to Her Majesty perfectly reflected everything Elizabeth II represented, and the finest British qualities of diligence, duty, service to others, resilience, humility, loyalty, courtesy, and good humour.
It’s that unifying force that is the Royal Family’s greatest asset because it brings out the best in us.
Whether they’re commemorating weddings or funerals, jubilees or national triumphs, the most striking thing about our Monarchy is the way it rises above scandal, political toxicity, and whatever else is going on in the world, to offer us all moments, however fleeting, of escapism, joy, fun and patriotism.
Yes, all the over-the-top palatial extravagance, pompous formality, weird outfits and rituals, and ludicrous antics of some of the royals, can sometimes feel like watching a never-ending episode of Blackadder.
But when I’m sitting outside Buckingham Palace today, co-anchoring the Coronation coverage for Fox News in America, I’ll be bursting with excitement and pride, knowing there is no other country that even comes close to being able to do what we do on these big royal days.
There’s been a concerted effort in the past few weeks to suggest this Coronation will be a damp squib compared to the one for Queen Elizabeth II.
All the usual royal-bashing killjoys have crawled out of their rocks to demand an end to the Monarchy and vent their furious spleens at having to call anyone King or Queen in this day, and age.
‘Give us an elected official as head of state!’ they scream.
To which my response is: what, like Boris bloody Johnson, who still goes by the title of ‘Right Honourable Gentleman’?
Or maybe they’d prefer the American system where the 2024 presidential choice could be a rematch of Biden/Trump with the former so old and doddery now he can barely remember what day it is, and the latter has been charged with criminal offences for paying hush money to a porn star?
On balance, give me someone like King Charles who has spent his entire life preparing for this job, and exudes an exemplary calmness, civility and wisdom gleaned from 70 years watching his mother do it better than anyone in history.
Fortunately, all the moaning and doom-mongering about the Monarchy has failed to dampen the spirits of the vast majority of Brits.
I walked through Westminster earlier this week and could feel a real sense of mounting Coronation fever.
The flags are out, the pub bunting is up, the streets are packed with people from all over the world - 100,000 tourists have come to London for the event – and it’s estimated there will be a £450 million boost to the capital’s coffers alone which is worth remembering when the republican nay-sayers whine about what a waste of money the royals are…
Meanwhile, all over Britain, families and friends are preparing to celebrate today in their own way – with village fetes and town fairs, house parties and pub knees-ups.
I’ll be honest, I thought the idea of everyone crowding round their TVs to recite an oath of allegiance to the new King was daft and borderline North Korean in its anachronistic thinking.
Not least because there’s not a cat in hell’s chance of me ever pledging my eternal fealty to his ‘heirs and successors’ if there’s even a remote possibility of that one day being either Prince Andrew or Prince Harry.
But I am definitely up for toasting Charles with a rousing cry of ‘God Save The King!’ when the crown is placed on his head at Westminster Abbey, and I’m sure most Britons will share my sentiment.
It’s easy in this social media era to get dragged down the rabbit holes of negativity about days like this and let the noisiest nastiest minority voices influence our thinking.
Or to allow a few idiot Just Stop Oil protestors spraying orange paint around to ruin the atmosphere.
But let’s just ignore them.
As my eldest son tweeted this week: ‘You may not care about the Coronation, but I can assure you that no one cares that you don’t care.’
Instead, I urge everyone to come together to mark this historic moment in British history, and to celebrate the fact that we still have by far the most popular Monarchy on Planet Earth and can still put on a show that is the envy of every other country.
Today, the eyes of the world will be upon us as our magnificent military roll out the largest procession since Queen Elizabeth’s Coronation in 1953.
It is going to be an awesome, stunning, memorable day.

And the world will see us at our absolute best.
They will see Great Britain.
author: Piers Morgan

https://www.thesun.co.uk/news/22241801/n.title: KING'S SHIELD Inside Britain’s most powerful warship which will guard London from drone attacks during the coronation
https://www.thesun.co.uk/news/22241801/n.text:
BRITAIN’S most powerful warship will stand guard on the Thames to shield the King — but police admit they are powerless to stop protesters aiming to ambush the Coronation.
HMS Diamond, a Type 45 destroyer has awesome firepower and radars that can deal with missiles and drones.
The radars can spot and track stealth targets the size of a cricket ball at three times the speed of sound — from 250 miles away.
They can guide up to 16 missiles simultaneously as they blast their way towards zig-zagging targets.
The Navy says the warship — which will be docked at Greenwich, South East London — is in the capital to “celebrate the Coronation”.
It is due to host a series of VIP cocktail parties and performances by the Royal Marines band.
But Naval sources say it would only take a “flick of a switch” to trigger its air defence systems.
The 500ft-long warship can carry up to 48 Sea Viper missiles.
The 16ft long missiles launch ­vertically from the ship’s foredeck.
They reach four times the speed of sound and “manoeuvre for the kill at G-forces no human can withstand”, the Navy says.
The might of HMS Diamond — which arrived at the Thames flood barrier yesterday — contrasts with the weakness of the law to deal with demonstrators.
A Met Police chief conceded that cops will be unable to prevent anti-monarchists waving placards on Saturday’s procession route — in front of a global TV audience of hundreds of millions.
It is feared eco mobs like Extinction Rebellion and Just Stop Oil will also try to disrupt events at the weekend.
Deputy Assistant Commissioner Ade Adelekan vowed that anyone suspected of criminal behaviour “camouflaged as protests” will be immediately arrested.
But he admitted: “Protest is lawful and the only time we can intervene is when it becomes criminal.
“If at any point the protest moves from being lawful to criminal then you will see extremely swift action.”
Hardline campaign group Republic say 1,700 of their members will be protesting in Trafalgar Square, on King Charles and the Queen Consort’s route from Buckingham Palace to Westminster Abbey.
A total of 11,500 police officers will be on duty in central London — the same number that guarded Queen Elizabeth’s state funeral last September.
Met chiefs revealed there will be even more visiting VIPs this time than at the funeral.
The police response to Coronation- related events — dubbed Operation Golden Orb — is being run by the Met in a bomb-proof operations basement near Waterloo.
It swung into action earlier this week when the Stone of Destiny was transported to London — to be placed under the Coronation chair.
On the big day, snipers will be in static positions.
For the first time on a state occasion, police will use live facial recognition cameras to try and pick out suspects in the crowd wanted for criminal offences.
But Britain’s liberal laws mean the cameras cannot be used on known terrorist suspects or agitators from climate and anti-royal groups.
Republic spokesman Graham Smith said that the group has had two meetings with the Met and numerous phone conversations.
He said: “They have repeatedly said they have no concerns about Republic’s plans.”
However, he said the group had received a letter from a Home Office police powers unit warning new legislation allows cops to arrest protesters “locking on” to railings or glueing themselves to roads.
However, Mr Smith said the group received a letter from a Home Office police powers unit warning that new legislation allows officers to arrest protesters “locking on” to railings or glueing themselves to roads.
He said: “It’s a mystery why the Home Office thought it necessary to send an anonymous letter that could be interpreted as intimidation.
“Republic will not be deterred and we will be protesting.”

Fears of a lone wolf Coronation attack were reinforced by the arrest of a man in a security scare at Buckingham Palace on Tuesday.
Mr Adelekan said the incident had been reviewed as part of the Coronation security plan and police were happy with arrangements.
